gh issue create --milestone "v1.1 Backlog" --label bug --label priority/P2 --title "Frontend OIDC: hardcoded offline_access scope likely breaks Cognito sign-in (invalid_scope)" --body "Found in the pre-apply review of the AWS track. \`frontend/src/auth/authClient.ts\` always requests \`scope = openid profile email offline_access [apiScope]\`. \`offline_access\` is not a Cognito scope (system scopes are \`openid\`, \`email\`, \`phone\`, \`profile\`, \`aws.cognito.signin.user.admin\`) and can't be added to \`allowed_oauth_scopes\`.

Per the [authorize-endpoint docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/authorization-endpoint.html), an unknown/invalid scope returns \`error=invalid_scope\` to the redirect URI (the docs also say unassociated scopes are \"ignored at runtime\" — the two statements conflict, and community reports of \`invalid_scope\` for un-enabled scopes are common, e.g. rancher/rancher#54127). If it errors, sign-in is dead on Cognito; if ignored, it works (Cognito issues refresh tokens on the code grant regardless of \`offline_access\`).

Needs a live check against a real pool (#953 rule). If it errors: make the scope list provider-tolerant — e.g. an optional \`DATAQ_AUTH_SCOPE\` runtime override, or drop \`offline_access\` when the discovery document's \`scopes_supported\` omits it." 2>&1 | tail -1; gh issue create --milestone "v1.1 Backlog" --label bug --label priority/P2 --title "AWS: github-deploy IAM policy's ecs:cluster condition denies RegisterTaskDefinition" --body "Found in the pre-apply review of \`deploy/terraform/aws/github_oidc.tf\` (#1342). The \`EcsDeploy\` statement puts \`ecs:RegisterTaskDefinition\`, \`ecs:DescribeTaskDefinition\` (and \`ecs:DescribeTasks\`) under an \`ArnEquals\` condition on \`ecs:cluster\`. Those actions don't populate the \`ecs:cluster\` condition key (task definitions aren't cluster-scoped), so the condition evaluates against a missing key → **implicit deny**. The future \`deploy-aws.yml\` would fail at its first \`aws ecs register-task-definition\`.

Fix: split the statement — cluster-scoped actions (\`UpdateService\`, \`RunTask\`, \`DescribeServices\`) keep the \`ecs:cluster\` condition; \`RegisterTaskDefinition\`/\`DescribeTaskDefinition\` move to their own statement (resource-level \`*\`, no cluster condition — that's the best available scoping for the task-definition action family). Harmless to fix before first apply; must be fixed before the deploy workflow exists." 2>&1 | tail -1

The frontend target group health-checks \`/healthz\`, which the nginx image **proxies to the api** (\`nginx.conf.template\` \`location = /healthz\`). So if the api is down, the ALB marks the (perfectly healthy) frontend targets unhealthy and ECS kills/replaces frontend tasks in a loop — masking the real failure and taking the static SPA (and its error page) down with it.

Also relevant to first bring-up: until \`deploy-aws.yml\` exists and rolls a current image, the services start on the create-time defaults \`backend :v10\` / \`frontend :v2\` — and \`:v10\` (2026-06-29) predates both \`OidcBearerScheme\` and \`SECRET_STORE=aws_secrets_manager\`, so the api/worker will crash-loop and the frontend will flap on this health check from the first minute after apply.

Fix options: health-check a static nginx path (e.g. \`/\` serving index.html, or a new nginx-local \`/livez\` stanza) so frontend health means \"nginx is up\", and keep api health observable via its own service/logs — or accept + document the coupling." 2>&1 | tail -1

content.text:
Review done — **verdict: NOT clean, so per your "iff all looks good" gate I did not run `tofu plan`/`apply`.** Five findings filed as issues #1345–#1349. Here's the full report.

## What I reviewed

All three merged changes end-to-end: [#1337](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1337)'s `AwsSecretsManagerStore` ([secrets.py](backend/app/core/secrets.py)), [#1340](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1340)'s `OidcBearerScheme` + config + MCP mode ladder ([auth.py](backend/app/core/auth.py), [config.py](backend/app/core/config.py), [mcp/auth.py](backend/app/mcp/auth.py)), and all 17 files of [#1342](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1342)'s [deploy/terraform/aws/](deploy/terraform/aws/) — cross-checked against the frontend's actual runtime auth contract ([authClient.ts](frontend/src/auth/authClient.ts), [config.ts](frontend/src/auth/config.ts), [nginx.conf.template](frontend/nginx.conf.template)), the Azure stack's container commands, and AWS's own documentation for the claims I couldn't settle from code.

## Blockers (why the apply is off)

**1. Cognito rejects HTTP callback URLs — the "HTTP-only ALB, no domain" and "Cognito" decisions are mutually incompatible ([#1345](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1345), P1).** AWS requires redirect URIs to be HTTPS except `http://localhost`. [cognito.tf](deploy/terraform/aws/cognito.tf) registers `http://<alb-dns>/auth/callback`, so the apply is expected to fail at the user-pool client — and even if it created, sign-in could never complete. Same issue also covers a second bug hiding behind it: the SPA's redirect URI is `${origin}/`, never `/auth/callback`, so the registered path is wrong regardless. This needs **your decision**: cheapest fix without buying a domain is CloudFront in front of the ALB (free default `*.cloudfront.net` HTTPS cert); the alternative is a domain + ACM. I didn't pick one because it un-locks a decision you locked.

**2. Cognito access tokens carry no `email` claim ([#1346](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1346), P1).** `_extract_oidc_claims` reads `email` off the bearer, but the SPA sends the *access* token, and Cognito access tokens have no email/name. Every user would provision with `email=""` — admin allowlist dead, and the **second** user to sign in hits the unique lower-email index and is permanently 409'd. The #1340 tests hand-built claims *with* email present — the exact fixture-encodes-our-model shape the project's #953 rule warns about. Suggested fix in the issue: fall back to the standard `userinfo` endpoint (provider-neutral).

**3. The SPA hardcodes `offline_access` in its scope request ([#1347](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1347), P2).** Not a Cognito scope; AWS docs say unknown scopes return `error=invalid_scope` at the authorize endpoint (with some conflicting "ignored at runtime" wording — needs the live check, but it's a real provider-neutrality gap either way).

**4. The GitHub-deploy IAM policy denies `RegisterTaskDefinition` ([#1348](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1348), P2).** The `ecs:cluster` `ArnEquals` condition covers actions that never populate that condition key, which evaluates to an implicit deny — the future `deploy-aws.yml` would fail at its first task-definition registration. Mechanical fix (split the statement); should land before first apply.

**5. First-boot reality + health-check coupling ([#1349](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1349), P3).** Until `deploy-aws.yml` exists, apply brings services up on the create-time defaults `:v10`/`:v2` — and backend `:v10` (June) predates both `OidcBearerScheme` and `SECRET_STORE=aws_secrets_manager`, so api/worker would crash-loop from minute one. Compounding it, the ALB health-checks frontend `/healthz`, which nginx *proxies to the api* — an api outage recycles healthy frontend tasks.

## What checked out (verified, not just skimmed)

- **Provider-neutrality of the backend**: `OidcBearerScheme` is genuinely generic — OIDC discovery + JWKS via PyJWT, no vendor SDK; alg pinned to RS256 (no alg-confusion), `kid` required, issuer verified, fail-closed on JWKS outage with a single refresh-retry, mutual exclusion with Azure enforced at boot, MCP mode ladder mirrors REST exactly. No Entra claims leak into route code. The one provider-aware line (Cognito `client_id`-vs-`aud`) is documented and flagged for live verification, as recorded.
- **Secrets architecture**: clean two-owner split — infra bootstrap secrets readable only by the *execution* role, the app's runtime prefix (`dataq/*`) granted only to task roles; the store's `rstrip("/")` + forced-`/` join lines up exactly with the IAM resource pattern; `ListSecrets`' unscopeable grant is correctly narrowed client-side with `startswith`. Outage vs not-found exception discipline preserved.
- **Security posture elsewhere**: no credentials in any tracked file; state encryption (pbkdf2/AES-GCM) with the passphrase handled correctly; `.gitignore` covers tfstate/tfvars/plans; GitHub OIDC federation with exact repo+environment subject (no stored keys); RDS `publicly_accessible=false` + TLS, ElastiCache TLS + auth token with the `/`-`"`-`@` exclusion handled; SGs are least-privilege (the task self-ingress already narrowed to 8000 by the pre-merge review); Redis pinned to 7.1 (consistent with the redis-8-is-new-attack-surface rule); Cognito password policy is strong.
- **Verified-benign**: worker/migrate commands match the Azure stack byte-for-byte; `rediss://` without explicit `ssl_cert_reqs` defaults to CERT_REQUIRED in kombu/redis-py, which works against ElastiCache's valid cert; frontend's unset `DATAQ_AUTH_API_SCOPE` falls back to the image's empty-string default; `assign_public_ip=true` is the documented no-NAT tradeoff with SGs doing the gating.

## Recommended order from here

1. You decide the HTTPS approach (CloudFront vs. domain+ACM) — everything in #1345 hangs on the final public origin.
2. Fix #1345/#1348 in the TF stack, #1346 (+#1347 verification hook) in code — normal PR flow.
3. Then apply, build `deploy-aws.yml`, roll current images, and live-verify the two Cognito accommodations against a real pool.

I've updated nothing in the repo itself — findings are all filed. Sources for the AWS-behavior claims: [Cognito authorize endpoint](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/authorization-endpoint.html) (HTTPS-only redirect URIs, `invalid_scope`), [CreateUserPoolClient](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito-user-identity-pools/latest/APIReference/API_CreateUserPoolClient.html), [rancher/rancher#54127](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/54127) (invalid_scope in practice).

    public_jwk["kid"] = "test-key"
    public_jwk["use"] = "sig"
    return private_key, public_jwk

    """Resolve `jwks_uri` from an OIDC issuer's discovery document.

    Synchronous and shared by both callers that need it: `OidcBearerScheme.
    load_config` below (wrapped in `asyncio.to_thread` — it must not block the
    event loop) and `mcp.auth.build_auth_provider` (genuinely synchronous —
    fastmcp's auth provider is built at **module import time**, before any
    async startup hook exists to call into). One implementation, not a
    sync/async pair that could quietly drift apart.

    response = httpx.get(f"{issuer.rstrip('/')}/.well-known/openid-configuration", timeout=timeout)

    Synchronous and shared by every caller that needs a discovery field:
    `OidcBearerScheme.load_config` below (wrapped in `asyncio.to_thread` — it
    must not block the event loop), `mcp.auth.build_auth_provider` (genuinely
    synchronous — fastmcp's auth provider is built at **module import time**,
    before any async startup hook exists to call into), and `fetch_userinfo`
    (#1346). One implementation, not a sync/async pair that could quietly
    drift apart.
    """
    response = httpx.get(f"{issuer.rstrip('/')}/.well-known/openid-configuration", timeout=timeout)
    response.raise_for_status()

# ── userinfo fallback (#1346) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Cognito access tokens carry no `email`/`name` (only sub/client_id/scope/…),
# so identity claims a token omits are resolved from the issuer's standard
# `userinfo` endpoint instead — provider-neutral: any token that already embeds
# `email` (Azure AD, Keycloak defaults, …) never triggers the round-trip.
#
# The cache is keyed by the token's SHA-256 (never the raw bearer — it must not
# sit in a long-lived dict a heap dump could read) and bounded: userinfo is one
# extra HTTP call per token per TTL, not per request.

_USERINFO_TTL_SECONDS = 300.0
_USERINFO_CACHE_MAX = 1024
_userinfo_cache: dict[str, tuple[float, dict[str, Any]]] = {}


def _userinfo_cache_get(token: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    entry = _userinfo_cache.get(hashlib.sha256(token.encode()).hexdigest())
    if entry is None or entry[0] < time.monotonic():
        return None
    return entry[1]


def _userinfo_cache_put(token: str, claims: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    now = time.monotonic()
    if len(_userinfo_cache) >= _USERINFO_CACHE_MAX:
        for key in [k for k, (expiry, _) in _userinfo_cache.items() if expiry < now]:
            del _userinfo_cache[key]
        while len(_userinfo_cache) >= _USERINFO_CACHE_MAX:
            # Still full after dropping expired entries: evict oldest-inserted.
            del _userinfo_cache[next(iter(_userinfo_cache))]
    _userinfo_cache[hashlib.sha256(token.encode()).hexdigest()] = (
        now + _USERINFO_TTL_SECONDS,
        claims,
    )


def _merge_userinfo(claims: dict[str, Any], userinfo: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """`claims` with `email`/`name` filled from `userinfo`, or None on sub mismatch.

    OIDC Core §5.3.2: the client MUST verify the userinfo `sub` matches the
    token's — a mismatch means the response describes someone else (an IdP bug
    or a swapped response) and the sign-in must fail rather than mint a user
    row from mixed identities.
    """
    if userinfo.get("sub") != claims.get("sub"):
        return None
    for claim in ("email", "name"):
        if not claims.get(claim) and userinfo.get(claim):
            claims[claim] = userinfo[claim]
    return claims


def fetch_userinfo(issuer: str, token: str, *, timeout: float = 5.0) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """The issuer's userinfo response for `token` — sync, for `mcp.auth` (#1346).

    Returns None when the provider publishes no `userinfo_endpoint` (it is
    RECOMMENDED, not required — the caller proceeds with whatever the token
    carried). Raises `httpx.HTTPError` on an outage: an unreachable endpoint is
    an outage to surface, never an empty identity (the ADR 0039 decision 6
    lesson applied to auth). The REST path (`OidcBearerScheme._verify`) does
    the same fetch through its own async client; both share the TTL cache.
    """
    cached = _userinfo_cache_get(token)
    if cached is not None:
        return cached
    endpoint = discover_oidc_config(issuer, timeout=timeout).get("userinfo_endpoint")
    if not endpoint:
        return None
    response = httpx.get(
        str(endpoint), headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}, timeout=timeout
    )
    response.raise_for_status()
    userinfo: dict[str, Any] = response.json()
    _userinfo_cache_put(token, userinfo)
    return userinfo

if token is not None:
        claims: dict[str, Any] = token.claims or {}
        # PAT path (ADR 0026): the verifier already resolved (and last-used-
        # stamped) the owning user; load it by id — no upsert, the user exists.
        pat_user_id = claims.get(PAT_USER_CLAIM)
        if pat_user_id:
            user = session.get(User, pat_user_id)
            if user is None:  # revoked/deleted between verify and tool call
                raise McpAuthError("could not resolve the API key's user")
            return user
        settings = get_settings()
        mode = mcp_auth_mode(settings)
        if mode == "generic_oidc":
            # `sub` — the RFC 7519 REQUIRED subject claim — not Azure's `oid`.
            # No guest-user policy here: that concept is Azure B2B-specific, and
            # the generic REST validator (`core.auth.OidcBearerScheme`) applies
            # none either.
            subject = claims.get("sub")
            if subject:
                email = str(claims.get("email") or "")
                name = claims.get("name")
                return _upsert_user(
                    session,
                    aad_object_id=str(subject),
                    email=email,
                    display_name=str(name) if name is not None else None,
                    oidc_issuer=settings.oidc_issuer,
                )
        else:
            # Mirror the REST validator's guest policy: reject Azure AD guests
            # (B2B / external) unless explicitly allowed, so /mcp can't accept
            # an identity the REST API would 403. The JWTVerifier already
            # validated signature / issuer / audience / scope; this is the
            # tenant-membership policy on top.
            if not settings.azure_allow_guest_users and is_guest(claims):
                raise McpAuthError("guest users are not permitted")
            # `oid` (the stable directory object id) is mandatory, exactly as
            # the REST resolver treats it — never fall back to `sub` (a per-app
            # pairwise pseudonym), which would key a divergent / duplicate
            # users row.
            aad_oid = claims.get("oid")
            if aad_oid:
                email = str(
                    claims.get("preferred_username")

# ── OidcBearerScheme: userinfo fallback (#1346) ──────────────────────────────
#
# Cognito access tokens carry no `email`/`name`; the scheme resolves them from
# the issuer's userinfo endpoint. These tests drive the REAL verify path with
# signed tokens — only HTTP is mocked.


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _clear_userinfo_cache() -> Any:
    auth_mod._userinfo_cache.clear()
    yield
    auth_mod._userinfo_cache.clear()


class _UserinfoTransport:
    """Serves /jwks.json + /userinfo, counting userinfo hits (cache assertions)."""

    def __init__(self, jwks: dict[str, Any], userinfo: dict[str, Any] | int) -> None:
        self.jwks = jwks
        self.userinfo = userinfo  # dict → 200 body; int → that status code
        self.userinfo_calls = 0
        self.userinfo_auth_headers: list[str] = []

    def handler(self, request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        if request.url.path == "/jwks.json":
            return httpx.Response(200, json=self.jwks)
        if request.url.path == "/userinfo":
            self.userinfo_calls += 1
            self.userinfo_auth_headers.append(request.headers.get("Authorization", ""))
            if isinstance(self.userinfo, int):
                return httpx.Response(self.userinfo)
            return httpx.Response(200, json=self.userinfo)
        return httpx.Response(404)


async def _scheme_with_userinfo(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
    issuer: str,
    jwks: dict[str, Any],
    userinfo: dict[str, Any] | int,
) -> tuple[auth_mod.OidcBearerScheme, _UserinfoTransport]:
    scheme = auth_mod.OidcBearerScheme(issuer=issuer, audience="dataq-client-id")
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        httpx,
        "get",
        lambda url, timeout: httpx.Response(
            200,
            json={"jwks_uri": f"{issuer}/jwks.json", "userinfo_endpoint": f"{issuer}/userinfo"},
            request=httpx.Request("GET", url),
        ),
    )
    transport = _UserinfoTransport(jwks, userinfo)
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        scheme, "_client", httpx.AsyncClient(transport=httpx.MockTransport(transport.handler))
    )
    await scheme.load_config()
    return scheme, transport


def _cognito_access_token(private_key: rsa.RSAPrivateKey, issuer: str) -> str:
    """The real Cognito access-token claim shape: client_id, no aud, NO email."""
    return _sign(
        private_key,
        {
            "sub": "cognito-sub-1",
            "iss": issuer,
            "client_id": "dataq-client-id",
            "token_use": "access",
            "exp": int(time.time()) + 3600,
        },
    )

    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:

    scheme, transport = await _scheme_with_userinfo(
        monkeypatch,
        issuer,
        {"keys": [public_jwk]},
        {"sub": "cognito-sub-1", "email": "olivia@example.com", "name": "Olivia"},

git add backend/app/core/auth.py backend/app/mcp/auth.py backend/tests/core/test_auth.py backend/tests/mcp/test_mcp_auth.py && git commit -m "fix: resolve missing OIDC identity claims from the userinfo endpoint

Cognito access tokens carry no email/name claim (only sub/client_id/
scope/...), so the generic-OIDC path provisioned every user with
email='' — WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS could never match, and the SECOND
user to sign in collided on uq_users_email_lower and was permanently
409'd (#1346).

Both validators now fall back to the issuer's standard userinfo
endpoint (discovered alongside jwks_uri) when the verified token lacks
an email:

- REST: OidcBearerScheme fetches through its own async client.
- MCP: resolve_current_user via a sync fetch_userinfo (same reason
  discover_jwks_uri is sync).
- Shared bounded TTL cache keyed by the token's SHA-256 (one HTTP
  round-trip per token per 5 min, never the raw bearer in a dict).
- Fail-closed on outage: an unreachable userinfo endpoint is a 401 /
  McpAuthError, never an empty-email upsert (ADR 0039 decision 6's
  outage-is-not-a-state lesson applied to auth).
- OIDC Core 5.3.2 sub check: userinfo describing a different subject
  rejects the sign-in.

Tokens that already embed email (Azure AD & most IdPs) never trigger
the round-trip; a provider publishing no userinfo_endpoint proceeds
with the token's own claims.

Fixes #1346
